title: Jimmu Guyot Synthetic Straight-Ray P-Wave Tomography Surrogate
summary: Derive rectangular-grid ray intersections from boundary endpoints, then recover a P-wave velocity surrogate from heteroscedastic active-source travel times and validate it on a hidden changed grid and ray geometry; this does not reproduce the paper's nonlinear joint inversion.
taskPrompt: Read input/tomography_case.json, input/profile_geometry.json, and input/problem_spec.md. The problem specification is authoritative for formulas and tolerances. Implement the prescribed diagonally preconditioned steepest-descent weighted straight-ray P-wave tomography solver with exact quadratic line search for the supplied grid (do not assume a fixed size), using km, seconds, km/s, and s/km. First derive each path-length row from source/receiver boundary coordinates by deterministic rectangular segment clipping, and independently compare that derivation with the staged path vector; do not consume arbitrary sensitivity coefficients. Write only output/model.json, output/trace.csv, output/report.json, and a reusable output/tomography_solver.py accepting --input CASE.json --output DIR. model.json must have exact keys grid, velocity_km_s, slowness_s_per_km, rms_s, ray_predictions_s with dimensions taken from CASE; trace.csv must include iteration,objective,rms_s,step and row-major s_0...s_{n-1} state columns, with at least four recomputed consecutive non-increasing finite objective rows; report.json keys are method,units,case_id,invariant. Use uncertainty_s as weights, positive velocities, a small ridge prior, no network, and standard-library Python only. The evaluator reruns the solver on a hidden changed grid, endpoints, crossing-cell geometry, ray count, and uncertainties. This is a bounded synthetic surrogate for the paper's P-wave observable, not its full nonlinear joint inversion.
agentMustDo: Implement an iterative weighted tomography solver and a reusable tomography_solver.py CLI.
Write model.json, trace.csv, report.json, and tomography_solver.py only under output/.
Use km, seconds, km/s, and s/km consistently; validate forward predictions and an independent RMS invariant.

evaluation: Hard gates independently validate every submitted forward prediction, RMS, velocity/slowness reciprocal, case/grid identity, units, weighted-ridge objective, and every intermediate slowness state/step in the auditable iterative trace against the input case. The visible model contributes 0.20*exp(-velocity_RMSE/0.20). The evaluator runs the reusable solver on a changed hidden case in an isolated directory containing only that case (hidden references are computed privately by the evaluator); hidden velocity RMSE contributes 0.50*exp(-RMSE/0.12), hidden forward-prediction RMSE contributes 0.25*exp(-RMSE/0.03), and hidden RMS agreement contributes 0.05*exp(-abs(delta_RMS)/0.01). Missing or failed hidden recomputation contributes zero. Passing threshold is 0.70.
